_readme: Monthly API budget for the AI newsroom (owner order 2026-09-01: never go
over budget again). budget_ledger.py records every desk's estimated spend
in originals/_ledger.json and paces the discretionary desks so the paper
never hits the provider cap and freezes like August. The briefs desk (the
wire) is never paced; it stops only at hard_stop_fraction of the budget,
keeping last-resort headroom under the real cap. Estimates run 10% hot at
list price on purpose.
THE OWNER'S KNOB is monthly_budget_usd — set it at or slightly below the
org's actual Anthropic monthly limit. Run `python3 budget_ledger.py
--forecast` before turning it: it says what the rest of the month buys at
this number and at the what-if levels.
THE PURSE (2026-09-02): allocations are WEIGHTS, not silos. The wire's
projected month is reserved first; the ceiling's remainder is the
discretionary pool, shared by weight. Each desk's cap accrues daily into a
purse; a run is allowed when the purse can pay for it, so a big run is
followed by saving up, never by a month-long blackout.
TIERS: a desk may list editions, highest first, each with the model, the
turn cap, a starting price (replaced by the learned median of its own
runs) and optionally the weekdays it may run. The governor picks the best
tier the purse can pay for that day. The editor's FULL edition is the
whole mandate on Opus; the LIGHT edition is the non-negotiables (breaking
sweep, stale sections, both press reviews, markets, running files) on
Sonnet. Change the days or prices here; never the budget without deciding.
MODEL POLICY (owner order 2026-09-12): the cheapest model that can do the
job. The wire's rewriting desk runs on Haiku 4.5 and is never upgraded; the
routine cycles (editor LIGHT, weekly maintenance) run on Sonnet 5; research
and the editor's FULL mandate run on Opus 5. Claude Fable 5.1 is reserved
for extensive research the owner dispatches by hand — no scheduled desk may
pin it, and this file may not name it in a tier.
ORIGINALS FIRST (cost review 2026-09-12): the paper was aggregating because
the desks that write could not afford to run. Measured over September: a
LIGHT edition produced 29 originals for $11.84 — $0.41 a bilingual story —
against $2.07 for an investigations report and $1.76 for a full edition.
The light edition is the cheapest originals engine by five times, so the
weights fund it first and the FULL edition drops to weekly (Monday). Days
with no editor run average 1.8 originals; days with a light edition, 11-18.
`--forecast` reports what each budget level buys in originals per day.
